requirement: During repository validation, Habeas MUST parse every first-party Rust source file: every `.rs` file among the sources reference discovery considers under {cite}`requirements.references.discovery`, except those under the project-root `vendor` directory. Every explicitly declared function or method, including trait methods and test helpers, and every struct, enum, and union MUST have a valid `{impl}`, `{cite}`, or `{test}` reference to a defined requirement or named example, or a valid citation of the built-in `habeas:none` under {cite}`requirements.references.no_requirement`, in a Rust comment attached to it or within its body. Comments belong to items under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`; a comment before a field, variant, or attribute inside an item belongs to that item. A named example MUST reference a requirement under {cite}`requirements.examples.definition`. A reference in a string literal, on an enclosing module or impl block, or only in an evidence input MUST NOT count for the items it encloses. Habeas MUST report every unreferenced item with its file, line, kind, and name, and MUST report a Rust parse failure instead of silently skipping the file.
rationale:
I found no gaps. Each obligation maps to code and to a test that asserts its outcome.

**Obligations and the code that carries them out**

- **Parse every first-party `.rs` file among the discovered sources, except those under the project-root `vendor` directory.**
  - `rust_files` in `src/rust_coverage.rs` keeps `.rs` files from the discovered sources and drops paths under `root/vendor`.
  - `validate_rust_functions` iterates those files. It is called from `inspect_repository_with_progress`, which carries the `{impl}`.
- **Every function or method (including trait methods and test helpers), struct, enum and union needs a valid `{impl}`, `{cite}` or `{test}` reference.**
  - `missing_function_references` walks every outline node of kind `fn`, `struct`, `enum` or `union`.
  - A node counts as cited when a comment run owned by it, or a closed fenced comment owned by it, holds a valid reference.
  - `ReferenceKind` has no `Fixme` variant, so a `{fixme}` reference cannot satisfy this check.
- **The reference must point to a defined requirement or named example, or be a valid `habeas:none` citation.**
  - The `counts` closure rejects `{term}` references and unknown names.
  - It accepts a built-in only if `builtin.check(kind, fenced)` passes. That check enforces the fenced form, a non-empty body and the `{cite}` role.
  - It accepts a requirement outright.
  - It accepts an example only if `example_references_requirement` finds a `{cite}` or `{test}` to a requirement.
- **A comment before a field, variant or attribute inside an item belongs to that item.** The outline comment-ownership code, covered by `requirements.references.outline_comments`, decides this. It is exercised by the struct and enum cases in the tests below.
- **A reference in a string literal, on an enclosing module or impl block, or only in an evidence input does not count.**
  - Only outline comments and comment fences are consulted.
  - Only the four item kinds are checked, and only references owned by that item count.
  - Evidence JSON is never parsed as Rust.
- **Report every unreferenced item with file, line, kind and name.** `validate_rust_functions` emits `"{label}:{line}: {kind} {name} has no requirement or example citation"`.
- **Report a Rust parse failure rather than skipping the file.** An `OutlineError` becomes `"{label}:{line}: cannot parse Rust source: …"`, and an unreadable file also gets an error.

**Tests**

- `finds_uncited_functions_without_using_enclosing_or_string_references` covers:
  - enclosing module and impl references
  - string and raw-string references
  - an unknown requirement name
  - a comment run across a blank line
  - a trailing comment
  - an inner doc comment
  - a body reference
- `checks_trait_test_helper_and_nested_functions_separately` covers trait methods, nested functions, test helpers and `{test}` references to an example.
- `an_example_counts_only_when_it_references_a_requirement` covers:
  - an example with no requirement
  - an example that cites only another example
  - an example that cites only a term
  - an `{impl}` on a term
- `structs_enums_and_unions_need_references_attached_or_inside` covers structs, enums and unions, including a comment before an attribute and field, a comment before a variant, and a nested struct. It asserts exact lines, kinds and names.
- `locates_functions_after_unicode_text` checks reported line numbers after non-ASCII text.
- `reports_all_files_and_parse_failures` covers:
  - scanning nested and `tests/` files
  - a parse failure
  - skipping `target`, `evidence`, `.git` and `book`
  - skipping a root `vendor` directory while still covering `src/vendor` and `src/book`
  - the error message format
- `fenced_references_in_comments_and_built_in_rules_are_validated` in `tests/references.rs` covers `habeas:none` cases: a valid fenced citation, an inline citation, an empty fence, the wrong role, an unknown built-in, and an unclosed fence.
- These tests cover discovery, parse failure and status output end to end:
  - `untracked_sources_are_not_validated_until_staged_and_status_lists_them`
  - `disallowed_paths_are_skipped_and_projects_outside_git_scan_every_file`
  - `discovery_errors_fail_before_configuration_or_inference` in `tests/authoring_batch.rs`
  - `status_preserves_repository_wide_rust_findings_in_every_form` in `tests/commands.rs`

**Marking and unspecified behavior**

- The code that implements the subject carries `{impl}` references: `missing_function_references`, `rust_files`, `validate_rust_functions`, `display_path`, `example_references_requirement`, `OutlineNode::display_name`, and the call site in `inspect_repository_with_progress`.
- The comment-ownership logic is marked under `requirements.references.outline_comments`.
- I found no unmarked implementing code and no unspecified observable behavior.

text: :::{req} rust_item_coverage

During repository validation, Habeas MUST parse every first-party Rust source file: every `.rs` file among the sources reference discovery considers under {cite}`requirements.references.discovery`, except those under the project-root `vendor` directory. Every explicitly declared function or method, including trait methods and test helpers, and every struct, enum, and union MUST have a valid `{impl}`, `{cite}`, or `{test}` reference to a defined requirement or named example, or a valid citation of the built-in `habeas:none` under {cite}`requirements.references.no_requirement`, in a Rust comment attached to it or within its body. Comments belong to items under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`; a comment before a field, variant, or attribute inside an item belongs to that item. A named example MUST reference a requirement under {cite}`requirements.examples.definition`. A reference in a string literal, on an enclosing module or impl block, or only in an evidence input MUST NOT count for the items it encloses. Habeas MUST report every unreferenced item with its file, line, kind, and name, and MUST report a Rust parse failure instead of silently skipping the file.
:::{req} discovery
Habeas MUST find the references of {cite}`requirements.references.roles`
throughout project source files and MUST fail with the source file and line if a
name has no matching `{req}` or `{example}` definition. In Markdown, escaped
roles and roles in code examples MUST remain literal. Reference discovery MUST
consider exactly the project sources that source-access policy permits under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.source_tools`: in a Git worktree, files present in
the Git index, including staged new files; outside Git, all project files; in
both cases excluding the project-root `book` and `evidence` directories, `.git`
and `target` directories at any depth, and paths disallowed by
{cite}`requirements.configuration.evidence_paths`. Evidence snapshots and
generated build output MUST therefore not be counted as source references.
:::{req} no_requirement
Habeas MUST provide the built-in `habeas:none` under
{cite}`requirements.references.builtin_definitions`, with this text:
> Cite this only when no requirement or example applies to the item under the
> reference procedure. The citation MUST use the fenced form, and its body MUST
> justify why the item exists. An item with an invariant worth checking, such as
> a cache that must not change results, needs a requirement stating that
> invariant instead. An item citing this MUST NOT implement end-user-observable
> behavior that no requirement specifies.
Only `{cite}` MAY reference it. Validation MUST report an inline citation of it
or a fenced citation whose body, without comment delimiters and other
references, is empty. Whether the justification holds MUST be assessed under
{cite}`requirements.references.citation_review`. `habeas status --all` MUST list
each `habeas:none` citation with its item and justification.
:::{req} outline_comments
Each documented profile defines which grammar nodes are comments; the Markdown
profile's comments are HTML comment blocks, so an inline HTML comment within a
paragraph is text of its section. In every supported language, comments on consecutive lines with no other source
between them MUST form one comment run. A comment that follows other source on
the same line, including another comment, MUST form a run by itself and MUST belong to the innermost outline node
containing that line. Any other run MUST belong to the next outline node that
starts after it within the smallest node containing it; when that container has
no such node, the run MUST belong to the container, which is the root node at top
level. A profile MAY bind a comment kind to its container
instead: such a run MUST belong to the smallest node containing it. The Rust
profile MUST bind inner doc comments (`//!`, `/*!`) to their container, so a
file-level inner doc comment belongs to the root node. A reference in a comment MUST count for the node its run belongs to under
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage` and
{cite}`requirements.references.authoring_inputs`.
:::{req} definition

An mdBook chapter MAY define an example with an opening fence of at least three colons immediately followed by `{example} <name>` and a closing colon-only fence of at least the opening length. The full name MUST use the same chapter-derived namespace and valid-name rules as `{req}`. The body MUST include all Markdown between the fences, excluding surrounding whitespace, and MUST describe a concrete case with expected behavior. An example MUST contain at least one valid `{cite}` or `{test}` reference to a requirement it illustrates; `{cite}` makes the requirement an input to the example's assessment, and `{test}` makes the example an input to the requirement's assessment, under {cite}`requirements.references.roles`. An example MAY use both. An example directive inside a fenced code block MUST remain literal.
